samples.text: Commuter bike maintenance

A steel touring frame with a 1x10 drivetrain, mechanical disc brakes and 35 mm tyres. Ridden
about 140 km a week, mostly on wet roads between October and March.
Every week

Wipe the chain with a rag and add one drop of wet lube to each roller, then wipe off the
excess after a minute. Check the tyre pressure: 60 psi in the front and 65 psi in the rear.
Squeeze both brake levers; they should stop a good finger's width from the handlebar.
Every month

Measure chain wear with the checker tool. Replace the chain at 0.5 percent stretch; at
0.75 percent the cassette wears with it and has to be replaced too. The current chain was
fitted in June 2025.

Check the disc brake pads. Replace them when the friction material is thinner than 1.5 mm.
Organic pads last about 1,500 km in winter on this route and twice that in summer.
Every six months

Clean and re-grease the headset and the bottom bracket threads. Replace the brake and gear
cables if they feel rough or the gears skip after adjusting the barrel. Check the wheels are
true and the spokes evenly tight.
Punctures

The tubes are 700x35 with Presta valves. A spare tube, two tyre levers and a mini pump live in
the saddle bag. Before fitting a new tube, run a finger round the inside of the tyre to find
what caused the puncture, or the new tube goes flat too.
Shop

The local shop on Mill Lane does a full service for 75 pounds, which includes new cables and a
wheel true. Book a week ahead in spring.
# Boiler service record

Combi boiler, wall-mounted in the utility cupboard beside the back door. Installed in March 2021
by Northside Heating, who hold the installation certificate and the commissioning checklist.
## Warranty

The manufacturer's warranty runs for seven years from the installation date, so it ends in
March 2028. It only stays valid if the boiler is serviced every twelve months by a registered
engineer and each service is logged with the manufacturer within thirty days. A missed year
voids the cover for any fault found after it, not only for faults caused by the missed service.
## Annual service

The service is booked for the first two weeks of October, before the heating goes on for the
winter. The engineer checks the flue, the gas pressure, the condensate trap and the expansion
vessel, and cleans the heat exchanger. Each visit takes about an hour.

| Date            | Engineer           | Notes                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 12 October 2022 | P. Adeyemi         | Condensate trap cleaned. System pressure topped to 1.2 bar. |
| 9 October 2023  | P. Adeyemi         | Expansion vessel recharged. Flue seal replaced.         |
| 14 October 2024 | R. Lindqvist       | No faults. Recommended a magnetic filter.               |
| 6 October 2025  | R. Lindqvist       | Magnetic filter fitted and cleaned. Pressure 1.3 bar.   |
## Pressure

The gauge on the front panel should read between 1 and 1.5 bar when the system is cold. Below
1 bar the boiler locks out with fault code F22. To top it up, open both filling-loop valves
under the boiler slowly until the needle reaches 1.3 bar, then close them fully. If the
pressure drops again within a week there is a leak somewhere in the system and the engineer
should be called rather than topping up again.
## Radiators

Bleed the radiators at the start of each winter, upstairs first, with the heating off and cold.
The bathroom towel rail has its own valve and takes longest to clear. After bleeding, check the
pressure gauge again: bleeding lowers it.
# Flat lease: the parts that matter

A plain summary of the tenancy agreement for flat 4, 18 Calder Road, written for my own
reference. The signed agreement is the one that counts if this summary and it ever disagree.
## Term and rent

The tenancy is an assured shorthold for twenty-four months, from 1 September 2025 to
31 August 2027. Rent is 1,150 pounds a month, due on the first of each month by standing order.
The landlord may raise the rent once, on the first anniversary, by no more than the change in
the consumer price index over the previous year, with at least two months' written notice.
## Deposit

The deposit is 1,325 pounds, held in a government-approved deposit protection scheme. The
scheme's certificate arrived by email on 9 September 2025. At the end of the tenancy the
landlord has ten days to propose any deductions, and anything disputed goes to the scheme's
free adjudication instead of being kept.
## Break clause

Either side may end the tenancy early from month twelve onwards with two months' written
notice. The earliest end date under the break clause is therefore 31 August 2026 if notice is
given by 30 June 2026. Notice has to be in writing; an email to the managing agent counts.
## Repairs

The landlord is responsible for the structure, the exterior, the boiler, the water heating and
the wiring. The tenant is responsible for small things: light bulbs, smoke alarm batteries,
blocked sinks caused by use. Anything urgent, such as a leak or no heating, is reported to the
managing agent's emergency line, which answers at any hour. Non-urgent repairs are reported by
email and should be acknowledged within five working days.
## Pets and subletting

One cat is allowed by name in the agreement. Subletting any part of the flat is not allowed,
and neither is running a business that brings visitors to the building.
## Leaving

At the end of the tenancy the flat has to be returned in the condition recorded in the
inventory of 1 September 2025, allowing for fair wear and tear. The carpets are to be
professionally cleaned only if they were cleaned before move-in, which the inventory says they
were.
# Cold room and freezers
How the cold storage on level 2 is run, for anyone covering the weekly checks.
## The units

| Unit | Kind               | Set point | Alarm above | Holds                                  |
| ---- | ------------------ | --------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------- |
| F1   | Upright, -80 °C    | -80 °C    | -70 °C      | Cell lines, plasmid stocks             |
| F2   | Upright, -80 °C    | -80 °C    | -70 °C      | Patient-derived samples (restricted)   |
| F3   | Chest, -20 °C      | -20 °C    | -15 °C      | Enzymes, antibodies in glycerol        |
| CR   | Walk-in cold room  | 4 °C      | 8 °C        | Buffers, media, bacterial plates       |
## Alarms

Each unit reports its temperature every minute to the building monitoring system. An alarm
sends a text message to the on-call technician and, after fifteen minutes unanswered, to the lab
manager. The alarm panel beside the cold room door is silenced and reset with the code
heliotrope-4417, which is changed every quarter and must never be written on the panel.

If a -80 °C freezer alarms, first check the door is fully shut and the seal is free of ice.
If the temperature is still rising, move the racks into the backup unit F1 or F2, whichever is
emptier, and log the transfer. A -80 °C freezer that has failed warms to -50 °C in roughly
four hours with the door closed.
## Weekly checks

On Monday mornings, record each unit's display temperature and the monitoring system's reading
side by side; a difference of more than 3 °C means the probe needs recalibrating. Scrape the ice
from the door seals of F1 to F3. Check the cold room's floor for condensation under the
shelves.
## Defrosting

The -20 °C chest freezer is defrosted every six months, in January and July. Its contents go to
the cold room shelf marked for it for no longer than two hours. The -80 °C units are defrosted
only by the service contractor.
# Lab safety induction
What every new member of the lab reads and signs before working at a bench.
## Before the first day at the bench

Complete the online biosafety course and the chemical handling course; both certificates go to
the lab manager. Collect a lab coat from the store room; coats never leave the lab, not even
for lunch. Safety glasses are worn whenever anyone in the room is working with liquids.
## Biological safety cabinets

Work with cell lines happens only inside a class II cabinet. Switch the cabinet on and let the
airflow run for ten minutes before starting. Wipe the work surface with 70 percent ethanol
before and after. Never block the front grille: the airflow through it is what keeps the
operator safe, and a full grille sets off the cabinet's alarm.
## Chemicals

Every chemical has a safety data sheet in the shared folder, and the risk assessment for a
procedure has to be read before running it for the first time. Flammable solvents live in the
yellow cabinet and never more than 500 ml at a bench. Acids and bases are stored apart.
## Waste

Sharps go into the yellow sharps bins, which are closed and collected when three-quarters full.
Biological waste is autoclaved before disposal; the autoclave log is signed by whoever runs
it. Chemical waste goes into the labelled containers in the fume hood, one container per waste
class, never mixed.
## Spills and accidents

Small spills of biological material are covered with paper towel, soaked in disinfectant and
left for twenty minutes before wiping. For anything larger, or any chemical spill that gives
off fumes, leave the room, close the door and call the lab manager. Every accident, however
small, is written in the incident book the same day.
## Working alone

No one works alone in the lab outside 8:00 to 19:00 on weekdays. Weekend work needs the lab
manager's approval and a second person in the building who knows you are there.
